title: The Button - VAVI Manufacturing Facilities and Headquarters / Mjölk architekti
text:
The Button - VAVI Manufacturing Facilities and Headquarters / Mjölk architekti

A few years ago, the architects began collaborating with Jirka Vávra and Katka Jiroutová, who took over management of the successful family business VAVI, founded by Věra Vávrová. After gaining experience at the Šumavan factory in Vimperk, Věra started small-scale shirt production with her husband. Under Jirka and Katka's leadership, VAVI grew into a respected Czech manufacturer of corporate clothing and men's and women's shirts, designing and producing its own collections while also custom-sewing for large companies and individuals. The brand outfits entire corporate teams, including international ones, from management to operations, with production largely concentrated in Vimperk and supplemented by facilities in Prague and elsewhere, all under a long-term emphasis on quality and craftsmanship.

title: Kingdee Tower / HENN
text:
Kingdee Tower / HENN

The Cloud Tower completes the existing Kingdee software park in Shenzhen's Nanshan neighborhood, which is an emerging tech district. Located on the edge of a green strip, the 211-meter-high tower provides space for offices, conferences and a restaurant for Kingdee, a leading provider of enterprise management cloudservices globally.

title: Bangbae Geunsaeng Neighbourhood Facility / aoa architects
text:
Bangbae Geunsaeng Neighbourhood Facility / aoa architects

For rental neighborhood facilities, it's essential to design a compact layout with simple, rectangular rental units and a core that includes the stairs, elevator, and restrooms. The elevator and other vertical circulation, which require more height, are placed on the south side where there are no sunlight restriction setbacks.

title: Phan Chau Trinh Sports Hall / scale50
text:
Phan Chau Trinh Sports Hall / scale50

The sports hall is part of an ongoing effort by Phan Chau Trinh Interlevel School to renew its infrastructure, gradually transforming its existing campus to accommodate the needs of both a growing school and the neighboring community.

title: Cella House  / iHouse estudio
text:
Cella House / iHouse estudio

Casa Cella is a weekend home located in El Pinar, Canelones, just a few yards from the beach. Designed for a family that loves hosting friends and extending daily life outdoors, the house is conceived as an open platform facing the garden, the barbecue area, and the pool, establishing a fluid relationship between the interior spaces and the landscape.

title: Cayucos Ridge Barn / Clayton Korte
text:
Cayucos Ridge Barn / Clayton Korte

Set along the eastern edge of a 150-acre property in California's Santa Lucia Range, 30 acres of which are planted with Syrah vines, this simple agricultural barn supports vineyard operations while honoring its unique Central Coast setting. Strategically positioned between the forest and vineyard, the 4,315-square-foot structure opens westward with broad bays, creating a direct connection to the working landscape. A generous roof overhang shades a functional work porch and shields the overhead doors from the intense afternoon sun, reinforcing the design's passive environmental strategies.

title: Powerwall / Studio RAP
text:
Powerwall / Studio RAP

Powerwall translates the invisible electromagnetic forces of a 150 kV switch station into a large-scale ceramic relief, giving the technical infrastructure of Beverwijk a tangible architectural expression.

title: Green by Law? Rethinking Sustainability and Architectural Responsibility Across Borders
text:
Green by Law? Rethinking Sustainability and Architectural Responsibility Across Borders

Sustainability in architecture is often discussed as though it were a universal standard—and, in principle, it should be. Buildings are increasingly evaluated through energy performance, embodied carbon, certification systems, material efficiency, biodiversity, and whole-life impact. Yet the rules determining what must actually be done remain highly local. A project designed in London, New York, or Copenhagen may be shaped by stringent energy codes, environmental review, disclosure requirements, planning controls, and increasingly ambitious carbon targets. The same practice working elsewhere may encounter a very different regulatory landscape.

title: Climate Experience World Visitor Center / DBCO
text:
Climate Experience World Visitor Center / DBCO

Germany's first visitor center dedicated to climate adaptation transforms its educational mission into an architectural experience shaped by landscape, material, and space.

title: Bothaus Coffee - Sudo Developer Center / HCCH Studio
text:
Bothaus Coffee - Sudo Developer Center / HCCH Studio

Located on the lower floor of Sudo Technology's office and robotics laboratory in a tower along Shanghai's Yangpu waterfront, Bothaus is a small reception and exhibition space designed for the embodied intelligence company and its invited users. At the outset of the project, the client introduced an unusual brief: the space should have a "low-tech feel". We found the phrase intriguing. Rather than simply describing an aesthetic preference, it seemed to suggest a broader idea of the future — one in which technology becomes increasingly embedded in everyday life, and increasingly less conspicuous.

title: Gandarillas House / Jose Pedro Vicente Arquitectos
text:
Gandarillas House / Jose Pedro Vicente Arquitectos

The proposal seeks to articulate the relationship between the site, the landscape, security, and the coastal climate. The entire program is elevated, while the ground level remains completely open. Rather than being occupied by the building, the ground becomes the primary space for outdoor living. The pool, gardens, terraces, barbecue area, fire pit, bar, and gathering spaces occupy the entire lot, allowing the open space to become the true heart of the living experience.

title: Aerocasa / Feliu Vega Kennedy Arquitectura
text:
Aerocasa / Feliu Vega Kennedy Arquitectura

First and foremost, this project is a garden and, second of all, a house. It is an inhabitable garden for someone seeking to escape the hustle and bustle of the world, to be lived in the tender company of their dogs and plants.

title: Mini Atalhada Building / SO Arquitetura & Design
text:
Mini Atalhada Building / SO Arquitetura & Design

Mini Atalhada results from the conversion and extension of a small storage building with a footprint of only 13 m², located in Atalhada, in the city of Lagoa, on the south coast of São Miguel Island, Azores. Set within a consolidated urban frontage and close to the sea, the building was acquired by the architectural studio to explore the minimum limits of contemporary living.

title: Match House (Art Omi) Temporary Installation / Young Projects
text:
Match House (Art Omi) Temporary Installation / Young Projects

Young Projects has a unique reputation for studying conventional material use and application, in order to reimagine new ways of employing the material. By iterating across scales of prototype, furniture, folly and eventually architecture, the investigations are carried out through meaningful collaborations between the studio and trusted makers and experts in their fields.

title: Alpamyr House / sandro durrer
text:
Alpamyr House / sandro durrer

As the last building before the expansive raised bog, Alpamyr occupies a special position in the landscape. It is an intergenerational house for two parties, characterized by its low rise and sensitive integration into the natural terrain, allowing it to blend quietly and unobtrusively with the surroundings despite its relatively large footprint. Two autonomous living units facilitate self-determined yet communal living across various life phases. Carefully placed openings frame views of the vast exterior world and create a connection between interior spaces and the landscape—retreats with a panorama that provide both contact and protection.

title: Architectural Heterotopias: Temporary Installations as Alternative Worlds
text:
Architectural Heterotopias: Temporary Installations as Alternative Worlds

While complex, layered with meaning, and categorized into various forms, heterotopia, a concept developed by the philosopher Michel Foucault, can broadly be understood as the manifestation of alternative realities. Unlike utopias – idealized, unreachable non-places – heterotopias are tangible, real-world spaces that operate according to their own internal logic, offering a lived alternative to dominant spatial and cultural paradigms.

title: Paris USMT Bizot Sports Centre / THINK TANK architecture
text:
Paris USMT Bizot Sports Centre / THINK TANK architecture

Located at 37 avenue du Docteur Arnold Netter in Paris's 12th arrondissement, the project transforms a former RATP industrial building into US Métro Bizot, a new sports center bringing together activities previously dispersed across several sites. Originally built to house horses during the era of horse-drawn transport, the building later became a mechanical workshop and storage facility before being abandoned.

title: How Architectural Fabrics Are Expanding the Role of the Building Envelope
text:
How Architectural Fabrics Are Expanding the Role of the Building Envelope

What can a textile do that glass, wood, concrete, or metal cannot? Architectural composite fabrics don't replace conventional building materials. Instead, they can complement them and often add another layer of performance to the building envelope. Their application changes with context. A composite membrane can become an exterior shading system for a tropical conservatory, an interior skin that shapes acoustics and spatial experience in a museum, or part of a facade strategy that improves the environmental performance of an existing building.

title: RSHP and ERRE Selected to Design New Valencia Central Station in Spain
text:
RSHP and ERRE Selected to Design New Valencia Central Station in Spain

The team led by engineering and technology group Sener, in collaboration with UK-based architecture practice RSHP and Valencia-based ERRE, has been selected to design the new Valencia Central Station in Spain. The proposal was chosen by Adif Alta Velocidad's Evaluation Committee following a competition for a new intermodal rail hub integrating high-speed, commuter, metro, tram, bus, taxi, and active mobility connections. The new infrastructure will be coordinated with the planned Central Park, the Access Canal project, and the future through tunnel. The scope also includes the refurbishment of the historic Valencia Nord Station, a designated Site of Cultural Interest, while preserving its architectural and urban heritage.

title: Cultural Center in Gisors / richter architectes et associés
text:
Cultural Center in Gisors / richter architectes et associés

The Gisor cultural center stands on a site that for many years remained at the margin of the town center. This made ground, serving as a car park, was an urban obstacle as much as a broken element of the landscape. Below its surface was a polluted mass of huge pre-war industrial infrastructures with underground water throughout and subject to flooding. These very conditions inspired the project. The architects have not sought to erase the constraints of the site, but rather to work with them and to turn them around so that a new urban geography could emerge.

title: Mecanoo and RDHA's Lawson Centre for Sustainability Opens at Trinity College With a Farm-to-Table Approach
text:
Mecanoo and RDHA's Lawson Centre for Sustainability Opens at Trinity College With a Farm-to-Table Approach

Mecanoo's Lawson Centre for Sustainability is the first new building for Trinity College since 1979. One of the most anticipated projects of 2026, it was designed to be one of Canada's most advanced sustainability-driven academic and residential buildings. Mecanoo worked in collaboration with Toronto architecture firm RDHA to design a sustainable community and "living lab," building on the College's traditions around shared meals and communal gatherings. Instead of the fourteen-story high-rise tower originally envisioned by the College, the team designed a walkable building that frames the existing campus and creates new landscapes for food production and social encounters. The broader campus vision included food, nature, work with local materials, and hands-on learning about sustainable living.

title: Asmara Heritage Project: Documenting a Colonial Project that Became Eritrea's National Symbol
text:
Asmara Heritage Project: Documenting a Colonial Project that Became Eritrea's National Symbol

Asmara, the capital of Eritrea, sits at over 2,300 meters above sea level on a plateau at the edge of the Great Rift Valley escarpment. Although situated in a country not known for large visitor numbers, the city has gained fame for its unique architecture. In July 2017, it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed as "Asmara: A Modernist African City," the first modernist urban site anywhere to be listed in its entirety, and Africa's first explicitly modernist World Heritage Site. Its heritage value came about as a result of a complex convergence of two aspects of Eritrea's history: an intense period of colonial construction as Italy pursued its imperial ambitions in Africa, and a long period of relative isolation that insulated the city from redevelopment.

title: Lorne Road House / Foomann Architects
text:
Lorne Road House / Foomann Architects

Lorne Road is a semi-detached Edwardian cottage. Renovated several years after its neighbour, the alteration is sympathetic to the heritage and contemporary buildings, and the calm and cohesive interior is subtly embellished with gentle curves, eclectic details and atmospheric light. The clients, a family of five, engaged Foomann to refresh the heritage part of their house and design a two-storey extension accommodating a new living space, playroom, main bedroom and mezzanine study.

title: Dong Trieu Retreat / NAQI & Partners
text:
Dong Trieu Retreat / NAQI & Partners

Dong Trieu Retreat is a collection of small structures nestled within the lush landscape of Quang Ninh, Vietnam. Originally conceived as a simple weekend retreat for a family from Ha Long, it gradually became their permanent home. Within this setting, we were entrusted with designing several spaces dedicated to restoration and renewal: a kitchen and dining area, a tea room, a sauna, and a meditation pavilion overlooking a water lily pond.
